next_step: Capacity planning workshop + SLA draft (schedule by AE). POC config for priority lanes.
notes:
-- Background / context:
  - Verdant Analytics: mid-to-large financial analytics platform building real-time advisor chat + scoring pipeline for client dashboards. Sensitive PII/derivatives data, bank integrations.
  - Evaluating Redwood Dedicated to get predictable throughput and hard latency SLOs; heavy interest in per-route priority lanes and tenant isolation.

-- Business requirements / ask (summary):
  - Throughput: steady-state 10k reqs/day ~ sustained 15 RPS with peaks up to 300 RPS for indexing windows; important for embedding bulk jobs + realtime chat.
  - Latency SLOs: P95 < 120ms for chat single-turn (<512 tokens); P99 target < 500ms. Background jobs (embeddings) can be best-effort but should not affect chat SLOs.
  - Reserved GPU planning: initial Dedicated cluster sizing ask = 8x A100-80GB equiv (region: us-east-1) with headroom for 2x burst nodes. Want vendor sizing worksheet + expected QPS per GPU under our token profile.
  - Traffic shaping / priority lanes: MUST have per-route priority lanes so that high-priority chat traffic is isolated from bulk embedding jobs. Mechanisms requested: per-route quotas, priority queues, token-bucket rate shaping, preemptive queuing/eviction for low-priority work.
  - Tenant isolation / noisy-neighbor controls: require per-tenant cgroup / GPU partitioning, request-level QoS weights, and admission control to prevent embedding spikes from saturating caches/GPU memory.
  - Observability: token-level cost breakouts, per-route latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), queue-length metrics, and per-tenant resource usage dashboards for billing and chargeback.
  - Security/compliance: customer-managed KMS preferred; SOC2 Type II report and pen-test results required. Data residency in us-east-1 only.

-- Technical notes from meetings:
  - 2026-02-10: load test (Fireflies ff_2026-02-10_verdant_capacity_test) ran with synthetic traffic. Findings: with default batching, chat p95 rose to 260ms when bulk embedding ingestion ran concurrently. Indicates need for strict traffic shaping OR dedicated GPU partitions for high-priority routes.
  - 2026-02-18: SE call (Priya) walked through packet-level mitigation ideas: separate worker pools, hard per-route request slots, dynamic token-bucket per-tenant, and KV-cache pinning for chat sessions. Verdant asked about preemption semantics: can low-priority batches be paused mid-batch? Redwood answer: depends on model/serving runtime; suggested model-fallback for degraded mode.
  - 2026-02-24: SLA negotiation prelim (ff_2026-02-24_sla_discussion). Verdant needs 99.95% availability for Dedicated, 24/7 support, and latency credits for p95 breaches. Legal pushed for clear definitions of maintenance windows and breach measurement intervals.

-- POC / milestone plan (agreed tentative schedule):
  - 2026-02-10: initial load test (done)
  - 2026-02-25: capacity planning workshop (scheduled)
  - 2026-03-04: deploy priority lanes config on Dedicated POC cluster (SE lead: Priya)
  - 2026-03-11: run mixed workload stress test (chat + embedding) and collect p50/p95/p99, queue metrics, and GPU utilization
  - 2026-03-18: legal & security review complete (target)

-- Proposed traffic shaping architecture (notes captured by SE):
  - Two logical lanes: high-priority (chat, auth flows) and low-priority (embedding indexing, nightly batch scoring). High-priority gets guaranteed slots on isolated worker pool; low-priority runs on separate pool with burst capacity and backpressure.
  - Request admission: token-bucket per-route + global fair-share controller. Token buckets assigned based on reserved throughput in contract.
  - Noisy-neighbor controls: enforce GPU reservations (N GPUs pinned to high-priority pool), cgroup limits for CPU/GPU memory, and per-tenant soft-limits on KV cache size.
  - Preemption: prefer pausing low-priority batch windows; if not possible, model-fallback to smaller variant or completion truncation.
  - Monitoring: alerts on queue length > X, p95 breach > 2x target for > 5min, and GPU utilization > 85% sustained.

-- SLA negotiation points to resolve (legal):
  - Define measurement windows (how p95 is calculated across priority lanes).
  - Compensation model: credits for latency SLO misses vs. downtime credits.
  - Maintenance: max 4h/month scheduled, notify 72h in advance.
  - Data handling: confirm keys are customer-managed (bring-your-own KMS / HSM).

-- Customer quotes & sentiment:
  - "We will not accept chat latency regression during our end-of-day indexing window" — VP Eng.
  - Tech lead: "If you can guarantee that high-priority lanes are unaffected by our bulk batch jobs, we'll move forward to procurement."

-- Next steps (short):
  - AE to schedule capacity workshop (week of 2026-03-01).
  - SE to produce GPU sizing worksheet and expected QPS per GPU under Verdant token profile by 2026-03-03.
  - Legal to send SLA mark-up draft; confirm SOC2 artifacts and pen-test timeline.
  - Run POC stress test and deliver metrics dashboard to Verdant by 2026-03-12.

  - Prioritize building a sample priority-lane config template for Dedicated (include per-route quota examples and RBAC for tenants).
  - Add observability alerts for cross-workload interference; include example queries for p95 by route and queue depth.
  - SE follow-up ticket: INF-1284 created to track POC config changes and stress test setup.
